<p>アラートは調査の入り口です。検知の重要度を参考に、端末の役割・ログ・予定さ:
An alert is the starting point for an investigation. Use detection severity as a reference, then compare the endpoint's role, logs, and planned work to form your judgment.

1. Collect evidence

Add to evidence from “Log search”, “Assets & records”, and “Contact”. Click an IP address or username to search for the same value. If useful, use grep or awk in the “Terminal”.

2. Record your response

Select a verdict, priority, subject, and response, then record the facts and remaining questions. An “Inconclusive; further investigation needed” verdict can also complete a case when supported by appropriate evidence and a handoff. The checks look for subjects, times, and evidence IDs in the report and a recipient in the handoff. The meaning of your writing is not graded automatically.

3. After the controls, try guided practice

Practice investigation through response in six dedicated cases. The first two provide the next action and its reason, the next two provide a checklist, and the fifth provides only an objective. In the sixth, use evidence to decide on endpoint isolation, then request it, verify the result, and hand off. All cases have no time limit and are saved separately from regular shifts. At the end of each case, compare your report with the example before continuing.

4. Time and difficulty

Low, Medium, and High each contain five different cases. Low requires basic evidence comparison; Medium requires multiple logs and business confirmation; High requires evaluating multiple endpoints or missing information. Low has no time limit and delivers one case at a time. Medium delivers five together with 20 minutes each. High adds a case every 45 seconds with 15 minutes each. Missing the initial-response deadline on a critical case ends the shift. Late completion of legitimate-activity cases is shown in the final results. These timings are training settings.

For a single Medium or High case, you can select “Investigate without a time limit from the start” before beginning. The two-case parallel exercise on Medium defaults to no time limit, so you can practice investigating another case while waiting for a reply. Regular five-case shifts and review after a timeout remain available.

“Advance to next update” moves past waiting time for replies or arrivals. On timed shifts, this time also counts toward deadlines. Shift elapsed time is separate from the event times (UTC) recorded in logs.

Saving and local operation

The app does not communicate externally. Autosave depends on the browser, so use “Export” to keep important progress in a JSON file. Use “Import” to move it to another browser. After a game over, you can retry or review without a time limit.
